articles.title: Redesigned Health app expands language support
articles.summary: Apple announced expanded language support for the redesigned Health app, bringing personalized health insights to millions of people worldwide.
bodyEvidence: Today, Apple’s redesigned Health app will expand language support to global English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), French, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Turkish, and Vietnamese, bringing powerful, personalized health insights to millions of people worldwide. 1 Built with Apple Intelligence at its core, the Health app dynamically adapts to an individual’s health metrics across iPhone and iPad, offering insight into how to optimize their day and a comprehensive view of long-term wellbeing. 2, 3 The Health app has been built to securely and privately protect a user’s data at every step.

The updated experience includes a new Insights tab that surfaces timely, holistic summaries spanning heart, sleep, readiness, fitness, vitals, and cycle tracking data throughout the day. A dedicated For You section delivers intelligent recommendations tailored to a user’s daily habits — such as practical guidance to adjust a wind-down routine following consecutive nights of interrupted sleep. The app pairs data with dynamic health content, offering educational videos and articles featuring Health app clinical experts.

To help users better understand their health trajectory, a new Longevity tab analyzes longitudinal metrics across heart health, sleep, mental wellbeing, movement, metabolic health, hearing, and nutrition. Central to this tab is Health Age, a feature that translates data from Apple Watch — including VO 2 max, resting heart rate, sleep, and heart rate variability — into a metric that reflects how a user’s body is tracking relative to their chronological age. Users can also incorporate clinical laboratory data, such as A1c and LDL cholesterol, to enrich their long-term health picture.

Additionally, the update introduces at-home movement evaluations, which make physical assessments accessible without requiring specialized equipment. Using an iPhone camera and Apple Watch, users can measure their flexibility, strength, balance, movement mechanics, and VO 2 max with real-time audio and visual feedback. Powered by on-device vision-based AI models and developed with clinical experts, the experience runs entirely on device; no video is ever recorded, stored, or shared.

The redesigned Health app is available in the iOS 27.3 developer beta today and will roll out to users as a free software update later this year. Apple will continue to expand support for the redesigned Health app in new languages.

articles.title: Apple unveils groundbreaking MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display
articles.summary: Apple today introduced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring breakthrough tandem OLED technology.
bodyEvidence: Apple unveils groundbreaking MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and Touch for the first time on Mac

The world’s best pro laptop now features an industry-leading tandem OLED display, an intuitive Touch experience, blazing-fast M5 Pro and M5 Max performance and AI capabilities, and up to 24 hours of battery life, all in a thinner, lighter design

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display , featuring breakthrough tandem OLED technology that delivers game-changing front-of-screen performance. Available in 14- and 16-inch models, MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display offers a visual experience unlike any other, transforming pro workflows with up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio for exceptional detail, a 120Hz variable refresh rate, and a wider color gamut covering both P3 and Adobe RGB for brilliant colors. The new MacBook Pro also introduces intuitive Touch capabilities on the Mac for the first time, opening up a whole new dimension for pros to interact with their content, from manipulating 3D models to playing musical instruments onscreen. The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, 1 Live Activities, and Siri AI. 2 And with up to 24 hours of battery life in thinner and much lighter 3- and 4-pound designs, MacBook Pro is more portable than ever, empowering pros to take their work wherever inspiration strikes. 3 Featuring M5 Pro and M5 Max, Apple’s most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and now up to 16TB of blazing-fast storage, the new MacBook Pro delivers speed and capability for the most demanding workflows. An enhanced six-speaker sound system now provides 50 percent deeper bass and remarkable sound clarity for even more immersive audio. And Thunderbolt 5 and a wide array of connectivity, a 12MP Center Stage camera, studio-quality mics, and the power of macOS 27 with Apple Intelligence and Siri AI complete the MacBook Pro experience. 2 It is available to pre-order starting today, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.

“The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is a monumental step forward for the Mac,” said Johny Srouji, Apple’s chief hardware officer. “PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display. It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of. And with the magic of Touch coming to MacBook Pro, combined with the game-changing performance of M5 Pro and M5 Max, we’ve created a whole new way for pros to interact with their content, taking their workflows to a completely new level. The new MacBook Pro is the result of the deep integration between Apple silicon, hardware, and software, and there’s simply nothing else like it.”

The new MacBook Pro debuts the PROLED XDR display, which uses tandem OLED technology and advances it with breakthrough innovations in every layer, advanced algorithms in the display engine, and a state-of-the-art factory calibration process to deliver Extreme Dynamic Range (XDR) and stunning visual fidelity. With exceptional brightness, striking contrast, and vivid true-to-life colors, PROLED XDR offers the ultimate front-of-screen performance, enabling a new level of visual acuity and precision for content creators, photographers, colorists, and designers who need a reference-caliber display on the go.

PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display, delivering true-to-life color and unparalleled brightness and contrast. The PROLED XDR display offers tandem OLED technology unlike any other, with deep innovations in its layers that keep brightness and grayscale uniform across the entire display, while minimizing internal reflections common in traditional OLED designs. It’s all backed by advanced algorithms in the display engine that precisely control each pixel in real time, plus a meticulous manufacturing process and precise calibration of every panel for consistency from display to display.

PROLED XDR offers up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, allowing specular highlights to shine with stunning intensity. And through optimizations in the tandem OLED panel and custom compensation techniques, combined with precise control of light across the display, the PROLED XDR display achieves an industry-leading 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, so even the deepest shadows reveal incredible detail, bringing HDR content remarkably close to reality.

The display engine precisely controls the color and luminance of every pixel at the sub-millisecond level, compensating for content, pixel use, temperature, and environment all at once to offer exceptional brightness uniformity and grayscale accuracy, even in fast-motion content. It also monitors and adapts each pixel’s usage over time to preserve stunning image quality. And ProMotion technology delivers adaptive refresh rates from as low as 10Hz for better power efficiency and up to 120Hz for fluid responsiveness for content in motion.

PROLED XDR offers pros a super-wide color gamut with P3 and now Adobe RGB — critical for workflows in photography and design — along with notably wider coverage in green and cyan ranges. This results in more than 80 percent Rec. 2020 coverage for HDR video editing and color grading. Cutting-edge factory calibration ensures luminance, white point, and color gamut are precisely aligned with standard targets. Both color spaces are accessible within a single default preset, streamlining pro workflows and making it seamless to switch between them. With the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, pros have a portable reference display on the go.

With up to 2000 nits peak SDR brightness, combined with a state-of-the-art antireflective coating, the display is easy to read even in bright lighting conditions. For even greater visibility, the nano-texture option — now precisely etched into the cover glass — further reduces reflections and glare to eliminate distractions while maintaining an excellent viewing experience.

With breakthrough tandem OLED technology, extreme brightness, and extraordinary contrast, along with a super-wide color gamut, PROLED XDR is truly the world’s best laptop display, giving pros an unparalleled visual experience and setting a whole new bar for the industry.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.

Apple apps are optimized for the new MacBook Pro, and many existing apps work with Touch right away, because macOS automatically translates touches into clicks. Updated system gesture APIs also enable developers to create intuitive experiences designed specifically for Touch. And a wide range of third-party apps that pros rely on every day will also take advantage of Touch on the new MacBook Pro, bringing new ways to interact with their favorite tools and workflows. These include everyday productivity and collaboration apps like Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook; powerful creative tools for photo and video editing like Adobe Lightroom and DaVinci Resolve; 3D modeling and animation apps like Blender, Maxon Cinema 4D, Maxon ZBrush, and Shapr3D; along with music apps like Algoriddim djay Pro. 4

The Dynamic Island comes to the Mac, serving as the new home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI, where users can quickly search for anything on their MacBook Pro, access real-time updates, or take advantage of Siri AI. 1 Just like on iPhone, the Dynamic Island provides a quick, intuitive way to see and interact with important information. Users can ask a question, pick up a phone call, or control music — all within easy reach. With Live Activities, users can now get timely updates at a glance, and can accept an AirDrop request or pause a song with a tap of their finger.

The new MacBook Pro is thinner and significantly lighter for even better portability. The 14-inch MacBook Pro now weighs half a pound less at 3 pounds, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro weighs just 4 pounds — 0.7 pounds lighter than before. 5 Both models feature a slimmer design enabled by OLED’s more efficient display stack, with the 16-inch model nearly a millimeter thinner and the 14-inch model half a millimeter thinner.

With slimmer display borders, the 16-inch display grows to 16.3 inches, while the 14-inch display delivers a more portable 14.2-inch design. 6 And a completely redesigned thermal architecture enables the same incredible sustained performance of M5 Pro and M5 Max, even in a lighter design, while redirecting warm air away from the display.

The new MacBook Pro features M5 Pro and M5 Max, Apple’s most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop. Both deliver phenomenal single- and multithreaded CPU performance, along with faster unified memory, giving users blazing speed for the most demanding workflows. M5 Pro offers game-changing performance for scientists, engineers, software developers, and creative pros tackling intensive projects, accelerating everything from compiling code and running AI tasks to sequencing DNA and editing multiple streams of 8K ProRes video. M5 Max is built for users who want to push the limits even further, including 3D VFX artists, AI developers, and film composers. With M5 Max, pros can run LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device and accelerate intense workflows across detailed visual effects, 3D animation projects, film scores, and 8K video post-production.

A powerful Neural Accelerator built into each GPU core lets users speed through AI workloads like running a coding agent with an on-device LLM. And users are able to power through advanced graphics-intensive tasks like rendering a complex scene in Cinema 4D with Redshift. M5 Pro and M5 Max each feature a GPU with enhanced shader cores and a third-generation ray-tracing engine, delivering more photorealistic lighting and faster renders for 3D modeling. Dynamic Caching optimizes on-chip memory to significantly increase GPU utilization, driving huge performance boosts for apps like Blender and Unreal Engine, along with AAA games.

The industry-leading six-speaker audio system in the new MacBook Pro features an all-new woofer design that provides 50 percent deeper bass and all-new tweeters that shape sound dispersion for remarkable clarity. Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos wraps users in immersive sound for music and movies, and studio-quality mics deliver clean, clear audio for calls, recordings, and voice commands. And for the first time, dedicated audio tuning for closed-lid use delivers exceptional sound quality when MacBook Pro is connected to an external display, so users can enjoy a premium audio experience however they work.

The new MacBook Pro packs features for the most demanding users. The PROLED XDR display offers calibration and industry-standard reference modes in a portable form factor, making MacBook Pro an indispensable tool for filmmaking, design, and even medical imaging. 7 And macOS makes the most of the graphics, memory, and machine learning capabilities of Apple silicon, so apps perform at incredible speed.

The new MacBook Pro includes three Thunderbolt 5 ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. In addition to the PROLED XDR display, it supports up to three external displays with M5 Pro and up to four with M5 Max. Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 provide fast, reliable wireless connectivity, and Touch ID enables a quick, easy, and secure login experience. With its fast-charge capability, MacBook Pro can charge up to 50 percent in just 30 minutes. 3 In addition, storage is now configurable up to 16TB.

The new MacBook Pro comes to life with macOS 27. In addition to Touch built for macOS 27, MacBook Pro includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across apps; and an expansive set of improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help pros find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence by using a dedicated keyboard shortcut to get help with a specific item. Pros can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.

Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Pros can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. Features users already rely on get even better with improvements to performance and search. Refinements to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.

The new MacBook Pro was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 55 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 45 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The new MacBook Pro is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Cross-app workflows and visual creation also take a major leap forward in Final Cut Pro. Editors can open any image from their timeline directly in Pixelmator Pro, take advantage of advanced editing tools, and save changes back to the project automatically — no reimporting required. Generate Fill automatically matches the lighting, perspective, and texture of the surrounding environment so edits blend in seamlessly, while built-in Super Resolution upscales the generated content so it stays sharp at any size. Logic Pro’s industry-leading Stem Splitter gets even more advanced, with the ability to isolate, replace, or rebalance drum parts without needing the original multitracks. Users can also unlock a new Producer Pack from the 20-time Grammy winner and visionary widely known as the King of Modern Salsa, Sergio George. Keynote introduces support for Keynote Interchange Format (.keyx), an open JSON-based bundle file format designed to be readable and accessible to external tools, developer workflows, and AI agents.

articles.title: Developers bring incredible new app experiences to iPhone Duo
articles.summary: Starting this Friday, iPhone Duo users can discover amazing apps and games optimized for the first foldable iPhone.
bodyEvidence: From streaming and gaming to creativity and productivity, developers worldwide are taking advantage of the unique capabilities of the first foldable iPhone

Starting this Friday, iPhone Duo users can discover amazing apps and games optimized for the first foldable iPhone. With an inner display that’s 50 percent larger than iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the flexibility to use iPhone Duo in a variety of poses, developers are enhancing their apps to create exciting new experiences for capturing and sharing memories, streaming entertainment, gaming, multitasking, and much more. Because both displays share the same aspect ratio, apps transition smoothly from the outer display to the inner display and scale proportionally, so users can pick up right where they left off. And with the breakthrough performance of A20 Pro and new capabilities for iPhone — including Split View — iPhone Duo helps users enjoy their favorite apps and experiences while staying productive wherever they are.

“The response to iPhone Duo from our developer community has been incredible, and we’re inspired by how quickly they’ve embraced its larger display and new ways to interact,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations. “From watching popular shows and content on the expansive inner display to multitasking across windows or playing console-quality games, developers around the world are reimagining what their apps can do. We can’t wait for users to discover these experiences beginning this Friday, with many more app experiences to follow.”

New editorial collections for iPhone Duo apps and games will go live on the App Store this Friday, with additional app updates rolling out throughout the year. Apps optimized for iPhone Duo are easy to identify with a Made for iPhone Duo badge on product pages across the storefront.

With the larger display on iPhone Duo, every show, movie, and match becomes a big-screen moment that still fits in a user’s pocket. Netflix makes finding great entertainment even more fun: Members can scroll through Clips on the outer display and then open iPhone Duo to keep watching on the large nano-texture inner display, with Clips switching seamlessly between a vertical or horizontal view.

“People watch Netflix in all kinds of moments, and we built our new experience to move with them,” said Tom Richards, Netflix’s senior director of Engineering. “From browsing Clips on the outer display to settling in with a favorite show on the inner display, the experience adapts as iPhone Duo opens, closes, or turns, so discovering something new and sitting down to watch it feels effortless.”

More streaming services — including Prime Video and Paramount+ — are joining Apple TV in using the larger canvas for movies and series. With iPhone Duo, Prime Video enhances the viewing experience for users as they stream premium entertainment, and when partially folded, content plays on the top half of the display while X-Ray details showing cast and bonus content appear on the bottom half. Paramount+ offers richer playback controls and expanded browsing for shows and live channels. When iPhone Duo is propped open on a table, users can easily enjoy content hands-free, without a stand. Sports fans can follow MLB and PGA Tour with live games and highlights, plus real-time scores, stats, and leaderboards on the larger display.

“Baseball fans are incredibly passionate about the sport, and they follow our games as closely as they can. Now, iPhone Duo provides an exciting new fan engagement platform by showcasing the action and information simultaneously,” said Kenny Gersh, MLB’s executive vice president of Media, Business Development, and Product. “This incredible device unlocks a fun, versatile way to experience baseball from anywhere, and we’re grateful to have worked with Apple to ensure the app is ready for the World Series. Set iPhone Duo on a table partially folded and the live game plays on the upright half of the display while real-time stats fill the half resting on the table, so fans never have to choose between the broadcast and the box score.”

With Split View, users can open two apps side by side on iPhone for the first time, and productivity apps are making the most of the extra room. In the coming weeks, Microsoft Word and Outlook will roll out a desktop-class experience in users’ pockets, placing Word’s formatting tools alongside a document and Outlook’s inbox next to a full message. Zoom turns the inner display into an immersive video conference room, so users can see shared content and other participants at the same time. Slack brings a user’s whole workspace into view, making it easy to follow channels and automate tasks. Salesforce helps teams manage customer relationships and act on business insights, with more of their dashboards in view.

Fantastical shows calendars, tasks, and menus together on the larger display, so users can take in more of their schedule at a glance. Note-taking and task apps are a natural fit for the larger canvas. Notewise brings notes, documents, and AI tools together in a single view, while Things and Bear make task management and organization simpler onscreen at once.

“Fantastical has always been about seeing your day at a glance, and iPhone Duo gives us more room to do that than any iPhone before it,” said Michael Simmons, cofounder and CEO of Flexibits, the maker of Fantastical and Cardhop. “With calendars, tasks, and menus visible together on the inner display, it feels like the full Fantastical experience from Mac and iPad, right in your pocket. And with Split View, you can easily look up contact details with Cardhop or plan your week right next to your inbox.”

The folding design of iPhone Duo unlocks new ways to capture and edit, and creative apps are following suit. Detail uses the new Core AI framework to run AI models on device, making content creation fast and easy on the large inner display. Instagram shows more posts and Stories onscreen at once, and with Instagram’s Edits , creators can view their full creative studio, including timeline, editing tools, video, and more. VLLO gives video creators more editing controls and footage onscreen at once.

“iPhone Duo gives us room to put the video and its transcript side by side, which is exactly how creators want to edit podcasts and interviews,” said Paul Veugen, Detail’s founder and CEO. “Editing on the inner display feels as natural as editing a document, and because our AI models run on device, captions, filler-word removal, and audio enhancement are fast and private wherever creators are.”

A20 Pro and a custom vapor chamber give iPhone Duo up to 35 percent better sustained performance than iPhone 17 Pro, so games look and feel great for longer gameplay sessions on the large inner display. In Asphalt Legends , players can race more than 350 cars against up to seven online opponents, with detailed cars and dynamic lighting filling the inner display. Zenless Zone Zero brings its fast-paced action to every way of holding iPhone Duo, with controls that adapt to each position, and UnGodly , a dark fantasy RPG from Azra Games, adjusts its controls and view for each display, including a taller view of its open worlds when iPhone Duo is closed. UnGodly launches on the App Store in November, and Zenless Zone Zero will be updated for iPhone Duo next month.

On Apple Arcade, Sneaky Sasquatch and Retrocade take full advantage of the folding display, delivering a uniquely immersive experience when opened, and convenient pick-up-and-play fun when closed — bringing to life the full versatility of iPhone Duo’s gameplay.

Independent developers are also finding playful ways to make the fold part of the fun. Deck-Man turns iPhone Duo into a retro cassette player: Users can open it to pick an album and insert the tape, and then close it to start listening with music from Apple Music .

“Asphalt Legends is all about speed and spectacle, and iPhone Duo lets players feel more of both,” said Raúl Orrego del Río, Gameloft’s game manager. “The large inner display and the sustained performance of A20 Pro let us put more of the track and every detail of our cars in front of users, so races look and feel incredible wherever they play.”

When iPhone Duo is partially folded and placed on a counter, NYT Cooking shows more detailed recipes with richer visuals, making it easy to follow along while cooking. LTK lets shoppers watch creators’ videos and browse the exact products featured in the same view, while Lowe’s lets home improvement shoppers take a closer look at finishes, materials, and design details. Shop shows more products in its feed, with more room to discover, buy, and track orders, in every pose. When it’s time to make dinner plans, OpenTable adapts its layout, keeping restaurant details, availability, and booking easy to navigate. DoorDash will make it easy to track a delivery on a larger map later this year. And Yelp puts maps and reviews side by side so users can discover and compare local businesses with ease without tapping back and forth.

“We’ve spent the past four years bringing more instructional and inspirational video into NYT Cooking, and iPhone Duo helps bring that work to life,” said Camilla Velasquez, New York Times Cooking’s general manager. “With iPhone Duo propped on the counter, users can follow each step, set timers, and watch their favorite recipe creators demonstrate techniques, all with more room to see what they need. It’s another way we’re making our recipes more accessible, so people at every skill level can feel more confident in the kitchen.”

Updated travel apps from leading brands help keep trip details close at hand. Lyft gives riders more room to compare ride options and see the route at the same time alongside a larger route map, and American Airlines places boarding passes, seat selection, and terminal maps within easy reach. United Airlines brings its navigation to the right side of the display, giving travelers quick access to booking flights, managing trips, and other helpful tools throughout their journey. Flighty offers a dedicated flight-tracking mode for when iPhone Duo is propped up, making it easy to keep an eye on a flight.

Stargazers can explore the night sky across the inner display of iPhone Duo with Sky Guide , which pairs edge-to-edge star maps with Liquid Glass controls, while Tide Guide brings tide charts and live weather radar into one view. DJs can mix on the go with edjing Mix , which gives them more room for two decks, audio effects, and one-tap stem separation, while Next Shot helps golfers find and preview courses with immersive imagery, plus detailed views of stats and scorecards.

In addition to many of these globally popular apps, developers around the world are bringing their most popular local apps to iPhone Duo, with experiences designed to take advantage of its larger display and versatile design.

In China, iQIYI offers more room to discover shows and films, and adjusts its playback controls to each position. WPS Office adapts its interface and controls to each position, making it easier to work on iPhone Duo, and Xmind brings mind maps and outlines together in a side-by-side view, letting users explore the big picture while working through the details. Weibo optimizes its feeds, videos, and posting tools for iPhone Duo, with layouts for reading, watching, and sharing when unfolded or partially folded. AMap adapts to the different poses of iPhone Duo, with a portrait view for the road ahead and a landscape view for the bigger picture. rednote provides more room to discover photos and posts, with layouts that adapt smoothly and a video view that brings playback and comments together on the larger display. Taobao takes advantage of the larger display to show more products, with zoom gestures to adjust the number of items per row and a side-by-side view of product images and details on the larger display.

In Korea, readers will be able to enjoy comics on WEBTOON and books on NAVER SERIES on a larger display. KakaoTalk lets users keep track of multiple chats and groups while diving into a specific conversation, without switching back and forth, while KakaoPage delivers an immersive, book-like reading experience with Split View. BAND gives communities more room to keep up with posts, events, and photo albums in a single space.

Across Europe, developers are bringing their apps to iPhone Duo. Airmail shows more of a user’s inbox and messages at once, without toggling back and forth. Craft offers more room across notes, tasks, and documents, with a style gallery and live preview appearing side by side when iPhone Duo unfolds. Tiimo features a compact view when iPhone Duo is closed for quickly checking plans for the day and ticking off tasks on the go. When propped up, it pairs a visual timer with notes and subtasks for hands-free routines and focus.

In Latin America, Tripsy tailors its app navigation for a seamless iPhone Duo experience, letting users plan trips in new ways, while SmartGym makes it easier to keep up with the next workout, displaying routines and exercise details side by side onscreen. Moises makes practice more immersive, letting musicians adjust vocals and instruments while following along with lyrics and chords.

iPhone Duo opens up a new canvas for app experiences, and developers are already jumping in. More than 2,000 developers have attended more than 50 in-person workshops in 19 cities around the world — and additional workshops in London, Mexico City, Montreal, Paris, and Toronto will give even more teams the opportunity to experience iPhone Duo firsthand to update their apps and games. Through a range of online and in-person programming, technical guides, and Apple Developer Forums, developers have access to Apple engineers and designers to ask questions, get answers, and follow the discussion about all things iPhone Duo.

Developers can easily adapt their apps for iPhone Duo using new and updated APIs in the iOS 27.1 SDK. Apps that use standard SwiftUI and UIKit components adapt automatically to each display, moving controls to the side within easy reach, expanding into multiple columns on the inner display, and nudging buttons away from the fold when iPhone Duo is partially folded. New arrangement and reserved region APIs help developers build custom layouts that split content across the fold or extend edge to edge, and the new hinge API lets apps respond to the angle of the display as iPhone Duo opens and closes. With scene accessories, apps can show content on both displays at once, like a teleprompter on the outer display for the person being recorded, and new camera APIs support selfies with the rear cameras and the first under-display camera on iPhone.

Device Hub in Xcode 27.1 lets developers open, close, fold, and rotate a simulated iPhone Duo to test their apps in every pose. Design guidance and a series of Tech Talks for iPhone Duo are available on Apple Developer , and developers can submit their optimized apps to the App Store now.

articles.title: Apple unveils the 2026 Designers of Tomorrow
articles.summary: Apple’s Designers of Tomorrow showcase returns to spotlight the best in emerging talent, this time focusing on the theme of presence.
bodyEvidence: Curated by Rodman Primack, the exhibition celebrates next-generation designers and how they integrated Apple products into their creative processes

Apple’s Designers of Tomorrow showcase, in collaboration with Design Miami, returns for a second year to spotlight the best in emerging talent, this time focusing on the theme of presence. Exploring what still holds the public’s attention amid the hurried pace of the modern world, designers Salem S. Charabi, Isabel Rower, Yoonjeong Lee, and Parafernalia (Genki Matsumura and Sebastián Zorrilla) crafted original works that invite reflection and aim to shift perspectives, engage the senses, and kindle curiosity.

“The theme was born from an honest recognition of just how busy our lives have become,” says Rodman Primack, the program’s curator and former longtime creative director of Design Miami. “In answering it, our designers demonstrate the power of objects to shape our physical environments and transform the human experiences that are possible within them.”

This year’s participants were handpicked by a jury of global design voices — including Alexandra Cunningham Cameron, Fabien Cappello, Jennifer Dunlop Fletcher, Minjae Kim, Hun Chung Lee, Marion Mailaender, Nifemi Marcus-Bello, Jennifer Roberts, and Apple’s Molly Anderson — for their storytelling, material innovation, and craft. Their work also highlights Apple’s dynamic role in the creative process, empowering designers at every level to capture, refine, and share their ideas with the world.

“Apple products continue to emerge as a through line so many extraordinary designers share, spanning disciplines, cultures, and processes,” explains Primack. “It’s a testament to how seamlessly these products and tools can integrate into any workflow.”
Ahead of the exhibition, which opens today at Hôtel de Maisons in Paris, the featured designers discussed their final pieces and the tools they used to bring them to life.

Egyptian Danish architect Salem S. Charabi blends old-world practices and the latest digital tools to create timeless pieces, and his Designers of Tomorrow project, The Emergence of Light , is no exception.

“Light is something we’re all instinctively drawn to, dating back to our earliest fires,” Charabi notes. “A lantern felt like the perfect encapsulation of this idea — a reflection of our capacity to light up the world.”

Charabi constructed the lantern’s veil from banana paper, applying Japanese methods to Egyptian palms. A delicate skeleton of meticulously stacked date palm fronds provides a satisfying contrast to the limestone base, which carries the traces of its own formation in its grooves. “Each strand is an octagon in profile — just 3 millimeters wide, split by hand, and carefully drilled,” Charabi explains. “The ends are then sharpened with a chisel to interlock.” Both the lamp and the audience’s attention are suspended by the same tension.

The resulting piece feels at once deeply natural and finely engineered. “For this project, every component had to be mapped out in detail,” Charabi says. “I sketched and did all the 3D modeling on my MacBook Pro. It was a complex process getting everything to fit just right — from the carving of the stone and the paper molds, down to the delicate base.”
By blending familiar forms with the unexpected, Brooklyn-based designer Isabel Rower cultivates presence and transforms everyday objects into active sensory experiences.

“The surface functions as a site for curiosity for me,” explains Rower. “People don’t always know what my pieces are made of, even as they’re touching them. It’s captivating when something that isn’t readily understood takes the form of a familiar object, like a table or teapot. It generates a kind of friction that brings you into immediate awareness of the objects we use every day.”

This intrigue is captured by her piece Padded Chair 1860 , whose dramatic proportions draw on 18th- and 19th-century papier-mâché furniture and objets d’art. Its high-gloss finish stands in sharp contrast to the beaded fringe lining the seat. “The ceramic beads make a sound when brushed, drawing attention to both the material and its form, turning the unconscious act of sitting down into a mindful encounter,” Rower says.

Apple is a fixture throughout her creative process. “I use iPhone to capture quick thoughts and document my process, AirPods Pro to listen to music, and MacBook Pro to build my personal visual archive,” says Rower. “I’ll also use Keynote to juxtapose ideas and explore the relationship between images and text.”
For Seoul-based designer Yoonjeong Lee, presence begins with quiet discovery. Through material transformation, she repositions overlooked background objects as central subjects.

Her piece New Form showcases a trio of worn-down pencils that have been given new life as nails. “I wanted to express this year’s theme through something small that we could all recognize — a shared experience,” Lee explains. “This story doesn’t carry some grand narrative. Instead, it takes a second look at the familiar to help you rediscover that which has been quietly forgotten.”

The base of the piece doubles as a wooden table and lamp. Sheets of paper serve as a lampshade, softly diffusing the light below, while the pencils hold them firmly in place. Applying her signature technique of building volume through repetition, Lee stacked roughly 5,000 thin sheets of veneer to construct the wooden base.

Lee’s focus on overlooked structural elements extends to her workflow, where she credits iCloud, AirDrop, and Notes for keeping her process seamless. “I often use iPad Pro and Apple Pencil to create a sketch and jot down quick thoughts, but it’s how my devices connect to each other that makes them, and all their flexible features, truly useful,” she explains.

Founded by Genki Matsumura and Sebastián Zorrilla, Parafernalia is a design studio that spans from Monterrey to Mexico City. The duo’s creative process is driven by constant dialogue, questioning, and iteration, often powered by FaceTime.

“For us, presence can take many forms,” says Matsumura. “We experience it with ourselves, with our surroundings, and with others. Our piece explores how all these expressions can coexist within a single object.”

Their piece MonoAmbiente 1 considers presence as both a personal relationship with one’s surroundings and a collective act. When closed, its acid-etched stainless steel surface forms a vast landscape. Its dual state invites the observer not only to examine it but to experience it. Once expanded, it reveals stools and a table, turning a distant scene into an intimate setting where two people can converse, play chess, or share a drink.

The project mirrors the studio’s workflow: two designers relying on iPhone and iPad Pro to trade sketches and track progress in real time. “We don’t share a physical desk. Our studio is iCloud,” Matsumura explains. By using Messages, FaceTime, and Procreate, they bridge the geographic gap. “Apple plays an integral part in how we think, design, and communicate. In many ways, it’s how we cultivate presence with each other.”

articles.title: Apple announces American Manufacturing Program partners for latest iPhone lineup
articles.summary: Apple announced new and expanded partnerships with American companies that are supplying critical materials and components for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro.
bodyEvidence: Apple announces new American Manufacturing Program partners for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro
From U.S. titanium to advanced camera technology, American suppliers are producing key components in the latest iPhone lineup
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced new and expanded partnerships with American companies that are supplying critical materials and components for iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro.

Through its American Manufacturing Program (AMP), Apple is partnering with Perryman Company, a Pennsylvania-based titanium producer, to supply titanium for Apple products, including iPhone Duo. Apple is also expanding its partnership with Qnity Electronics, headquartered in Delaware, to produce technology for the new variable aperture in the iPhone 18 Pro camera system — the most advanced Apple has ever made.

Apple works with suppliers in all 50 states and supports more than 450,000 American jobs. Last year, the company deepened that commitment by launching AMP, aimed at bringing even more advanced manufacturing and critical component production to the United States as part of Apple’s $600 billion, four-year commitment to U.S. manufacturing and innovation.

“We’re thrilled to expand our work with companies producing advanced materials and components for our newest iPhone lineup right here in America,” said Sabih Khan, Apple’s chief operating officer. “American ingenuity is vital to all our products, from the titanium crafted for iPhone Duo to breakthrough camera innovations in iPhone 18 Pro. We’re proud to work with Perryman and Qnity Electronics to continue expanding our American Manufacturing Program and support U.S. jobs.”

The grade 5 titanium enclosure on iPhone Duo is exceptionally strong, providing amazing durability to the first foldable iPhone. Apple will commit up to $100 million over the next three years with Perryman, a family-owned business and a global leader in manufacturing specialty titanium products. At its site in Houston, Pennsylvania, Perryman melts, forges, and rolls titanium with a minimum of 80 percent recycled content for iPhone Duo.

Apple is also expanding its partnership with Qnity Electronics to build key camera technology for iPhone 18 Pro in the U.S. Qnity, which joined the American Manufacturing Program in March, will produce advanced films essential to the new variable aperture camera system on iPhone 18 Pro. Variable aperture is at the heart of the new 48MP Fusion Main camera, which enables incredible light and depth control. It’s powered by on-device intelligence that automatically lets in more light for darker settings and helps get sharper detail in brighter ones.

Nearly 100 components in iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro — from wireless chips to the silicon that powers key functions across the devices — are produced by American companies and drawn from suppliers in more than a dozen states. That footprint continues to grow, empowering partners across the country to bring new capabilities online:

As part of Apple’s ambitious goal to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030, all direct suppliers are required to power their Apple manufacturing with renewable energy by the end of this decade. These partnerships, which also include the increased use of recycled materials, reflect that broader environmental commitment.

Apple’s commitment to American manufacturing extends to the workers and businesses building the sector’s future. In August, Apple opened its Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston, Texas — the company’s second U.S. manufacturing learning site. Inside the 20,000-square-foot center, Apple engineers train small- and medium-sized businesses on the same processes used to make Apple products, from advanced manufacturing principles for final assembly to design considerations for printed circuit board assembly. The AMC sits within the same Houston facility that builds Apple’s advanced AI servers and will begin manufacturing Mac mini this year.

Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.

Three native flowers he encountered in the region — spiky green Echinops, flutelike pink trumpets, and wild yellow tulips — became the heart of this latest collection, inspiring 10 striking looks and three custom-built hot-air balloons.

For Aydın, Les Benjamins represents the intersection of people and their cultures, and “From Earth to Sky” is no different. Born in Germany, the designer was raised with what he describes as “German discipline and Turkish heart” — a duality that runs through his work. “The canvas is the West; the paint is the East,” he says of a collection that combines contemporary silhouettes with Turkish fabrics and Silk Road influences.

iPad Pro with the powerful M5 chip became the creative nexus for the entire project. After research trips, Aydın would assemble photographs, fabric references, and early designs in the Freeform app, where evolving mood boards could be easily shared or exported to keep work ticking along. “Freeform allowed me to bring my team into my creative journey instead of simply giving them finished ideas,” he says.

The multitasking features on iPad Pro became integral as the workflows multiplied. Aydın could use its intuitive windowing system to work on an active sketch in Procreate, refer to photos from his travels, and research local flora in Safari, all while Background Tasks exported files for his collaborators.

And then there were the hot-air balloons. Working in Procreate, Aydın and his team designed a single structure as a starting point, then rapidly duplicated, altered, and redrew it until three final forms emerged from dozens of variations.

An avid gamer, Aydın compares his relationship with Apple Pencil Pro to the muscle memory he developed while playing his favorite titles. Squeezing, double-tapping, and switching to the eraser now feel like reflexive actions, which enabled him to move quickly through variations without the tool interrupting the idea. “We were working on high-resolution images, creating multiple layers and playing with textures. That’s usually when things start to slow down,” he says. “But that never happened on iPad Pro. It felt just like working on a desktop.”
Back in Rose Valley, months of planning and work are finally coming to life.

Working with iPhone 18 Pro Max brings the immediacy Castillon loves as a director. “When I see something beautiful, I want to film it right away,” he says. Just as Aydın’s show travels from past to future, movement drives Castillon’s visual treatment. Custom-built drones each carry two iPhone 18 Pro Max models, with their 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide cameras focused on enhancing the sense of vertiginous speed while fitting the massive balloons into frame.

He uses ProRes RAW to preserve flexibility for color grading in post-production, as Cappadocia’s pale hues meet saturated pinks, yellows, and greens. “I’m a huge nerd for color, and the tones are really accurate on iPad Pro,” he says.

While his team records video, Castillon shoots stills with the 48MP Fusion Main camera, using the new texture and grain controls in Photographic Styles 3 to bring some of the tactile character he loves in analog photography into the images.

As feeds from the whirling drones come into Castillon’s production control center, synchronizing them begins right there on location. He reviews footage and makes selections on MacBook Pro with M4 Max; its nano-texture display helps reduce glare from the sun overhead.

With the performance in full swing, Castillon’s focus switches from crane to drone to capture the opening look: a Turkish caftan and a tree branch representing Anatolia, an homage to Turkish rock icon Barış Manço. The show’s scale is huge, but Aydın believes its potential is larger still.

For him, “From Earth to Sky” is a chance to bring Turkish culture to a global audience without losing sight of its roots. “I see my role as that of a translator and a bridge between East and West,” Aydın says. “I hope this project makes Turkish people proud.”

That energy efficiency improves network deployment economics when rolling out tens of thousands of sites. For a nationwide buildout, power draw at each location compounds quickly, and many tower sites face significant power constraints.

Maybe the most interesting part will be whether SpaceX can accelerate deployment of its 5G network, as it has with its AI compute build-out.

articles.title: Marvell Proposes Acquiring Lumentum to Combine Optical Circuit Switching with AI Connectivity Silicon
articles.summary: Marvell announced its intention to acquire Lumentum in a $115B acquisition to further optical connectivity in the AI era The post Marvell Proposes Acquiring Lumentum to Combine Optical Circuit Switching with AI Connectivity Silicon appeared first on ServeTheHome .
bodyEvidence: Marvell Technology announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied value of about $115 billion. The proposed deal aims to merge Marvell’s electrical interconnect and custom silicon portfolio with Lumentum’s high-performance lasers, optical circuit switching (OCS), and compound semiconductor manufacturing capabilities. For AI infrastructure designers facing the physical limits of copper, this combination could drive deeper co-design across the entire signal chain, from distributed data centers to connections within advanced semiconductor packages.

The primary driver for this acquisition is the industry transition from electrical to optical connectivity as AI clusters scale. At the Marvell Computex 2026 Keynote , CEO Matt Murphy described connectivity as the next major bottleneck in data center design, noting that compute performance gains are outpacing connectivity and networking gains. Marvell has positioned itself to address this by offering solutions across various distances, from long-haul coherent links to short-reach scale-up domains. However, the “copper wall,” or the maximum distance copper can viably support before signal integrity fails, is moving closer as lane speeds increase. A copper-to-optics transition is underway in the industry, albeit slower than many people thought it would be 10 years ago.

Marvell’s existing portfolio addresses parts of this challenge with products like the COLORZ 800 module, which we examined in Going 800Gbps at up to 1000km with the Marvell COLORZ 800 . That module uses coherent detection and a local oscillator to maintain signal integrity over vast distances, packaging complex DSPs and photonics into a standard OSFP form factor. While effective for long-reach scale-across links, the move toward co-packaged optics (CPO) requires even tighter integration between the switch silicon and the optical engine.

The proposed combination pairs Marvell’s electrical and optical interconnect, CMOS/silicon photonics, switching/custom silicon design, and packaging expertise with Lumentum’s specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing, including indium phosphide (InP), plus high-speed and high-power lasers.

As we saw in our Marvell TX9190 CPO switch coverage from OCP 2025 , near-package optical engines shorten the electrical path, with fiber runs and pluggable light sources replacing long PCB traces. We also saw some neat technology on our recent AWS Networking Lab tour .
By acquiring Lumentum, Marvell intends to control more of this supply chain internally and design solutions across a larger domain instead of having to go to different companies for different parts.

Beyond component integration, Lumentum brings optical circuit switching (OCS) to the combined portfolio. The Lumentum R300 OCS establishes direct optical paths between endpoints using micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) mirrors, eliminating intermediate packet processing and optical-electrical-optical (OEO) conversion along those switched paths. Lumentum says this results in dramatically lower latency, higher signal integrity, and significant reductions in network power for large GPU clusters.

Acquiring Lumentum and its technology will not come cheap, however. The $115 billion deal is being financed entirely with Marvell’s stock, significantly leveraging the value of the roughly $175 billion company in order to pay for the deal. In effect, this makes the deal closer to a merger than a buy-out. Following the settlement of the deal, Marvell shareholders will own 67% of the new company, while Lumentum shareholders will own the other 33%. Similarly, the deal will see three members of Lumentum’s board of directors join Marvell’s board, bringing it up to 10 members.

This deal, expected to close in the first half of 2028, so some time away, coordinates Marvell electrical and optical interconnect plus silicon design with Lumentum lasers, optical manufacturing, and OCS. The companies intend closer co-design and optimized, pre-validated optical solutions, faster time to market, and high-volume production, but that close is a long way away. This is a huge deal when companies are seeing valuations soar due to AI demand.

articles.title: Qualcomm Validates HBC Stacked Memory Ahead of 2027 Dragonfly AI250 Sampling
articles.summary: Qualcomm today is announcing that they have completed initial validation on their High Bandwidth Compute technology. The DRAM-stacked-upon-compute architecture moves on to commercialization, with Dragonfly AI250 set to sample in the first half of 2027 The post Qualcomm Validates HBC Stacked Memory Ahead of 2027 Dragonfly AI250 Sampling appeared first on ServeTheHome .
bodyEvidence: Qualcomm this morning is announcing that it has completed the initial validation of its High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) memory architecture, which will be a central part of the company’s upcoming Dragonfly data center AI accelerators. The stacked memory architecture will see Qualcomm and its manufacturing partners place multiple layers of DRAM on top of a small compute die in order to bring memory even closer to the compute hardware that is accessing it, allowing Qualcomm to reap the energy efficiency and cost efficiency benefits of a closer hardware placement.

The recent validation of the technology moves HBC one step closer to deployment in commercial products, which are scheduled to start sampling next year. Qualcomm has now validated that the technology works and is delivering energy efficiency and memory bandwidth close to their expectations, allowing them to move towards mass production next year while keeping customers (and investors) in the loop on the development of Qualcomm’s Dragonfly AI250 accelerator and its successors.

First announced by Qualcomm back at their 2026 Investor Day , HBC is a new Qualcomm-spearheaded technology that is intending to use near-memory compute in order to strike a new balance between memory capacity, memory performance, and production costs – with Qualcomm looking to push the envelope on all three aspects.

Fundamentally, the technology is a further variation on HBM and other memory stacking technologies. But unlike HBM where multiple DRAM dies are stacked on top of a base die that is connected back to the host processor over an ultra-wide memory bus, HBC aims to cut out the middleman by placing a small compute die at the bottom of the stack instead.

In principle, placing memory on top of a compute die has several benefits. The biggest of these is energy efficiency, as moving data around costs energy – and moving large amounts of data large distances costs even more energy. By placing memory on top of a compute die, this eliminates even the relatively short distance of an HBM connection (to say nothing of external memory like LPDDR5X), minimizing the amount of energy spent to move that data around. Those energy savings, in turn, can be funneled back into improving performance of the chip itself, or allowing a larger number of chips to be clustered together within the same energy footprint.

The compute die itself is not a full processor. But by placing the most memory bandwidth-intensive operations on the die and then sending the results from that back to the larger compute die at the center of the processor, Qualcomm is looking to get their memory and compute hardware as close together as is feasible.

Qualcomm’s efforts are also eyeing production costs here. Because of the wide memory bus used by HBM, it requires advanced packaging such as CoWoS or EMIB to connect HBM stacks to a compute die and memory controllers. But by shifting most of the computational workload to the compute die that sits under the memory, far less bandwidth is needed to connect the compute die to a larger processor die elsewhere on the chip package. And, consequently, that connection can be built with cheaper technologies such as traditional 2D organic substrates.

That said, HBC does not eliminate all of the complexity. Like HBM, it still requires bonding multiple DRAM dies (or in Qualcomm’s case: wafers) on top of another die using TSVs, which is itself a challenging process. Which means the need for complex manufacturing techniques has not gone away, but it has been reduced from both memory stacking and high speed chiplet connectivity to just the memory stacking.

Finally, Qualcomm is looking to strike a better balance between memory bandwidth and memory capacity here. Notably, the company’s HBC design calls for using LPDDR5X DRAM dies rather than the thin, high-performance dies used by HBM. The company has not outlined what the final performance of the technology will be, but the capacity of an HBC stack is already projected to be larger than what current HBM4 implementations can achieve.

Qualcomm’s fundamental argument through all of this is that HBC provides a better all-around solution than any other memory architecture, be it HBM, on-die SRAM, or off-package LPDDR. As proposed, HBC has strengths and weaknesses versus all of these technologies, but as Qualcomm argues, they can achieve memory bandwidth (and thus performance) far better than external LPDDR – and approaching HBM – without the capacity constraints of using on-die SRAM, or the high costs of the latter of those two solutions.

Ultimately, all of this is meant to lead to allowing Qualcomm to build a better chip for AI inference by meeting inference’s need for memory bandwidth and capacity with fewer drawbacks than existing technologies.
Diving into the validation process itself, for their initial HBC validation Qualcomm has hooked up an early HBC sample stack to a test unit in their San Diego labs.
While the test setup itself is not much to look at, inside of it is a chip that, for Qualcomm, is critical to their data center plans.

Given that this was an early sample, it should be noted that HBC stack they were working with here just had 2 layers of DRAM dies. Shipping products will have 4 layers. So Qualcomm is not yet at the point where they are testing full-sized stacks.

Briefly outlining their validation approach, Qualcomm tells us that they used the HBC test stack with an automated tester, which was used to measure the stack as both an LPDDR5X device and as an HBC device.

Ultimately, Qualcomm had three major findings with their successful validation testing. The first, of course, being that this worked at all, proving that it can be done. Meanwhile in regards to performance, Qualcomm measured their HBC solution as delivering more than five-times the energy efficiency (on a bandwidth-per-watt basis) than HBM4 as per its own specifications. Finally, while the company is not disclosing specific bandwidth figures, they are categorizing the measured bandwidth at 18x higher than external LPDDR5X.

The energy efficiency figure in particular is a bit short of Qualcomm’s initial projections for the technology, where they were hoping to beat HBM by 6x. But if this carries over to a full product, it still represents a significant improvement in efficiency.

According to Qualcomm, their validation testing also includes the thermal behaviors of the product, though the company has not gone into any further detail there. Qualcomm has had little to say on the subject so far, but thermal considerations are one of the major technical hurdles they will need to overcome, as a more active compute die as the base die in a stacked memory architecture is expected to put out more heat.

With their initial HBC validation complete, Qualcomm is now looking at moving on to the next step of commercialization of the technology with their Dragonfly AI250 accelerator. The successor to the Dragonfly AI200 accelerator due this year, AI250 will be the first product to integrate HBC – and it will be a key part of future Qualcomm AI accelerators after that. AI250 does not have a launch date yet, but according to Qualcomm it will begin sampling in H1 of this year, which is potentially a move-up for the company’s plans following the initial announcement that sampling would take place earlier this year.

If everything pans out with HBC, the technology will not be limited to Dragonfly AI accelerators, either. Qualcomm has previously announced that they would also be bringing the technology to their consumer-focused Snapdragon products – though the company is not specifying when and what products at the time.

Ultimately, HBC is a play for energy efficiency and a lower TCO for Qualcomm. If the technology pans out, the company expects to be able to deliver AI inference accelerators that are both more energy efficient and cheaper to build than contemporary designs. Which in turn would make them cheaper to operate (and ideally, cheaper to acquire) than GPUs for large AI inference operations. We will get to see how that plays out over the coming months as Qualcomm moves towards sampling Dragonfly AI250 in the first half of next year.

articles.title: NVIDIA Updates Rubin GPU Specs as First Production Hardware Arrives
articles.summary: As production hardware starts shipping, NVIDIA has updated some of the specifications for its Rubin GPU platforms The post NVIDIA Updates Rubin GPU Specs as First Production Hardware Arrives appeared first on ServeTheHome .
bodyEvidence: As we roll into the fourth quarter of 2026, NVIDIA and its partners are in the middle of the Vera Rubin ramp-up, including hyperscalers making some of the first NVL72 systems generally available to their customers . With Vera Rubin reaching the tipping point of its production roll-out, NVIDIA is also finally locking down the hardware shipping specifications. As it turns out, the company has quietly revised those specifications, with the Rubin GPU now offering less memory and scale-up networking (NVLink) bandwidth than NVIDIA previously promoted, but more scale-out bandwidth.

As initially spotted by IT Home , back in September NVIDIA posted the updated specifications for its Rubin GPU and various Rubin-based products on their webpages and in NVIDIA’s architecture datasheet. To be sure, it is not unusual for server hardware specifications to change before a product’s launch, especially for something like Vera Rubin, which was announced nearly a year in advance. NVIDIA’s case is no different, with the company previously noting that those specifications were preliminary and that “all values are up to and subject to change” at the time.

First, let us talk about NVIDIA’s Rubin GPU. The cornerstone of NVIDIA’s ambitions for this generation, NVIDIA’s Rubin server GPU will find its way into systems big and small and serve as the building block for much larger projects.

Compared to NVIDIA’s preliminary specifications, the HBM4 memory bandwidth for a single Rubin GPU has been revised down notably. NVIDIA was initially targeting 22TB/second of memory bandwidth per Rubin GPU. At 8 stacks of HBM4 memory, that meant running each stack at about 10.75Gbps/pin. But with these revised shipping specifications, a single Rubin GPU will now provide 19.2TB/second of bandwidth, for a data rate of about 9.375Gbps/pin, a net loss of 1.375Gbps, or roughly 11%.

This spec change comes as NVIDIA has been projecting some very aggressive data rates for HBM4. The super-sized version of the high-bandwidth memory specification already doubled the memory bus width per stack from 1024 bits to 2048 bits. At the same time, the official specification called for HBM4 stacks to run at a slightly lower clock rate than HBM3E, targeting 8Gbps/pin. NVIDIA’s 10.75Gbps rate was significantly higher than the original HBM4 specification, and even their newly reduced 9.375Gbps data rate is still quite a bit above.

For context, NVIDIA’s rival AMD will run its HBM4 stacks on the MI455X at only 7.6Gbps/pin . So NVIDIA’s revised targets are significantly higher than those of some other HBM4 consumers. Even after the news broke, NVIDIA has not said why it revised the memory bandwidth specs down. In lieu of that, the immediate assumption is that NVIDIA and its memory partners cannot deliver on those specs, be it memory controller speeds, memory stack speeds, memory stack yields (how many can run at the desired speed), or perhaps a combination of all of those factors. Regardless of the reason, the net result is that customers will have less GPU memory bandwidth at their disposal, with performance ramifications.

NVLink interconnect bandwidth is also taking a hit compared to NVIDIA’s original expectations. The preliminary specification for NVIDIA’s multi-GPU connection and scale-up fabric was for 3.6TB/second of NVLink bandwidth for each Rubin GPU. That is now a flat 3.0TB/second, a 600GB/second (or 17%) reduction. NVLink is an area where NVIDIA pushes hard to make many physical GPUs act as one, so it usually pushes the limits of what is possible.

While NVLink (scale-up) bandwidth has been reduced, scale-out networking bandwidth is now overperforming. For a single Rubin GPU, NVIDIA is offering 450GB/second of networking bandwidth, up from their preliminary specification of 400GB/second.

Beyond these changes, NVIDIA has not changed any other specifications for Rubin GPUs. The theoretical (on paper) compute throughput remains unchanged at 50 PFLOPS of FP4 inference and 35 PFLOPS of FP4 training. So NVIDIA has hit its clock speed and memory-capacity targets for the GPU.

Rubin’s spec changes will also affect all the products it will go into, most notably NVIDIA’s flagship Vera Rubin NVL72 rack. NVL72 showcases all of NVIDIA’s technologies, integrating its Vera CPUs, BlueField-4 DPUs, and, of course, Rubin GPUs.

For NVL72, its specifications have been revised in lockstep with the changes to a single Rubin GPU. That means that cumulative GPU memory bandwidth has gone from 1,580TB/second to 1400TB/second for the rack-scale system, a net loss of 180 TB (11%). Though, as with a single Rubin, the GPU memory capacity for NVL72 remains unchanged at 20.7TB of HBM4.

NVLink bandwidth across the system for its scale-up domain has also been adjusted. NVIDIA’s plans to offer 260TB/second of bandwidth across the rack have been revised down to 216TB/second, a 17% reduction matching the new 3TB/second rate of each Rubin GPU.

The silver lining for NVL72 is that it gets the same scale-out networking bandwidth boost as the individual Rubin chips. So whereas NVL72 was originally slated to offer 28.8TB/second of networking bandwidth, that has been dialed up to 32.4TB/second (bidirectional). This means that for larger deployments that make heavy use of scale-out networking, more bandwidth (and ideally, more performance) is now available than NVIDIA first projected.

Past this, the rest of the figures for Vera Rubin NVL72 remain unchanged from the earlier specifications. Whether an NVL72 rack can hit quite the same level of AI performance with less memory and NVLink bandwidth as originally intended seems doubtful, but the GPU compute hardware (and its CPU counterpart) is shipping at spec.

Finally, separate from the specification changes to the base Rubin GPU and the NVL72 rack, NVIDIA has also revised its other products built from Rubin. This includes the Vera Rubin Superchip, the Vera Rubin NVL4, and the HGX Rubin NVL8 products. The last one is getting a special mention here because, on top of the Rubin spec changes, it is getting a further change of its own.

On top of GPU memory bandwidth and NVLink bandwidth reductions, NVIDIA is also cutting back the amount of HBM4 memory available in NVL8 systems. These systems were originally set to come with 2.3TB of HBM4, but that is now down to a flat 2.0TB, losing 300GB (or 13%) of GPU memory.

NVIDIA’s preliminary figure would require each Rubin GPU in an NVL8 to be a full Rubin with its complete complement of 288GB of HBM4 available. However, a 2.0TB setup means each GPU needs only around 250GB of HBM4 available. That, in turn, requires only 7 of the GPU’s 8 HBM4 memory stacks.

Consequently, NVL8 is taking the biggest memory bandwidth hit of the entire Rubin family. Rather than losing just 11% of its memory bandwidth, it is losing 26%, or about 46TB/second. Each Rubin GPU would only have 250GB to 252GB of memory available, for 16.8TB/second of bandwidth per GPU.

Inference performance remains unchanged, at 400 PFLOPS for FP4, but FP4 training performance has been reduced from 280 PFLOPS to 270, and FP8 training has similarly been dialed down from 140 PFLOPS to 130. The 8-way Rubin systems do get the same network bandwidth improvement as the rest of the Rubin lineup. That figure has gone from 1.6TB/second to 1.8TB/second.

Finally, these changes affect both versions of the HGX NVL8, as well as DGX systems based on the NVL8 platform. Both the HGX Rubin NVL8 (Rubin + x86 CPU) and the HGX Vera Rubin NVL8 (Rubin + Vera) are subject to the same GPU changes.

It seems NVIDIA has had to rein in its ambitions for the Rubin GPU to bring the product to market at the scale they are aiming for, dialing back both GPU HBM4 memory bandwidth and NVLink networking bandwidth. The full ramifications of these changes are unclear at this time since not all workloads are bottlenecked by memory or networking bandwidth in the same way. In some respects, it is academic, since these changes apply to all shipping Rubin hardware from day one. Still, there will be a lot of NVIDIA Rubin deployed over the next few quarters.

articles.title: Counterpoint：三季度全球 DRAM 营收逼近 2000 亿美元，同比大增 369% 实现超级周期
articles.summary: p data-vmark="0000" IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，市场研究机构 Counterpoint Research 今日发布的《全球内存市场追踪》报告显示，2026 年第三季度全球 DRAM 市场营收接近 2,000 亿美元 span class="exch-money-value " （IT之家注：现汇率约合 1.34 万亿元人民币） /span ，同比增长 369%，接近去年同期的 5 倍。 /p p data-vmark="a766" Counterpoint Research 指出，此轮 DRAM 市场增长主要由价格上涨推动，而非出货量大幅增加。当季 DRAM 单位出货量环比仅增长约 4%，每 Gb 平均售价则达到 1.9 美元。 /p p data-vmark="3e4c" 高级分析师 Jeongku Choi 表示，本轮行情属于价格推动的超级周期，而不是出货量周期。“AI 已经将内存从普通大宗商品转变为高价值稀缺资源，买家当前的核心动作是争抢供应而非议价，在价格持续上涨的背景下，存储厂商下一季度将再创新的盈利纪录。” /p p data-vmark="0003" 分厂商来看，三星电子以 38% 的市场份额稳居 DRAM 市场第一；SK 海力士环比营收增长超过 DRAM，长期供货协议也为价格提供支撑。此外，主要厂商的新晶圆厂预计要到 2028 年才会开始投产，供应紧张局面或将延续。 /p p data-vmark="d286" “海量需求推动 DDR、LPDDR 的平均售价创下历史新高，二者营收同比分别增长 500%、近 400%。我们观测到服务器 CPU 相关内存消耗正在显著提升，这将进一步推高明年每 Gb 的均价，同时给终端市场带来压力。” /p

articles.title: 内存涨价环境下 Discord 弃用 Electron：改用 Rust 重写客户端，占用体积从 4GB 降至 290MB
articles.summary: p data-vmark="c48d" IT之家 11 月 5 日消息，Discord 联合创始人兼首席技术官斯坦尼斯拉夫 · 维什涅夫斯基（Stanislav Vishnevskiy）今天在 X 上确认，Discord 已弃用 Electron 并正在用 Rust 重写桌面客户端，界面层采用 GPUI 框架。 /p p data-vmark="c7cd" 他同时表示，移动端也将逐步迁移至 Rust，iOS 和 Android 版当前使用的 React Native 将被替换，但移动端保留原生 UI，通过 Rust 与桌面端共享应用代码。 /p p data-vmark="9634" 他在 X 上分享的一张 Windows 11 任务管理器截图显示，一个名为“Discord Phoenix”的进程占用内存 290.2 MB。他随后说明，该截图中的客户端同时登录了两个账户（新客户端支持账户多开）。相比之下，旧版 Electron 客户端在空闲状态下通常占用 1 GB 至 2 GB 内存，极端情况下可达 4 GB。 /p p data-vmark="d5a7" style="text-align: center;" img src="https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/11/cf0628ae-f9e4-43f7-ba9b-d054236a2757.png" w="898" h="824" data-mpos="2,0" data-weibo="0" data-snap-from="%7B%22from%22%3A%22x%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fx.com%2Fsvishnevskiy%2Fstatus%2F2118081920194203799%22%2C%22qualityMode%22%3A%22auto%22%2C%22qualityValue%22%3A%22original%22%7D" data-vmark="69bc" class="no-alt-img" /p p data-vmark="b073" 实际上，Discord 去年就已承认 Windows 客户端的资源占用问题。2025 年 12 月，一名 Discord 员工在 Reddit 上确认，公司正在测试一项机制：当内存占用超过 4 GB 时自动重启客户端。 /p p data-vmark="ecd7" 当时 Discord 表示，正常使用下内存应低于 1 GB，并已定位和修复多个内存泄漏场景，高负载下的 P95 内存占用下降了约 5%。 /p p data-vmark="face" IT之家注：P95 指将用户内存数据从低到高排序后位于 95% 位置的数值，即排除最极端 5% 情况后的高负载水平。 /p p data-vmark="f6e9" 公开资料显示，Electron 的资源开销源于其架构：每个 Electron 应用都打包一份完整的 Chromium 浏览器内核，而非像 WebView 那样与系统浏览器共享资源。Discord 被认为是优化较差的 Electron 应用之一，打开服务器或长时间使用后内存持续攀升。 /p p data-vmark="64be" 新客户端没有选择同样基于 Rust 的 Tauri 框架。Tauri 调用操作系统 WebView 渲染界面，虽能避免打包 Chromium，但仍依赖 Web 引擎。Discord 最终采用的 GPUI 由 Zed 编辑器团队开发，是一款 GPU 加速的 Rust 原生 UI 框架，不依赖 WebView 或 Chromium 进行界面绘制。 /p p data-vmark="aac3" 维什涅夫斯基表示，新应用仅在 YouTube 和 Activities 等嵌入内容场景调用系统 WebView，应用本身是原生的，外观和操作与现版保持一致。 /p p data-vmark="22f5" 维什涅夫斯基将“让整个客户端都跑在 Rust 上”称为一直以来的目标，并称新客户端“很快”将进入面向用户的测试阶段，但未给出正式发布时间。目前 Discord 官方尚未另行发布公告。 /p
